sections.caption: Two agents so far, across eight domains.

sections.value: One page for every agent I build. I expect this to run across healthcare, finance, go-to-market and e-commerce over time, so I gave it somewhere to grow rather than a page I would have to rebuild at the tenth entry.

The domain list is fixed and written down. A domain with nothing in it says what I would want from an agent there before I'd put one up — a citation on every clinical claim in healthcare, ground truth I can score against in finance. I would rather show the gap than pad the page.

Each agent gets a page of its own: what it does, the loop it runs, the tools it can call and what those tools can change, what I measured, and who wrote it. Two agents are up so far. One is mine. The other is Anthropic's commerce-agents, which I mirrored to read closely — its page says so, in the same line and the same type as mine, because a portfolio that quietly lists someone else's repository beside its own is worse than one that lists nothing.

Adding an agent is one JSON object in a single file. A small script checks it before it ships: it won't take a missing licence on someone else's work, a result quoted without its caveat, or a leftover TODO.
